events.input: $ for p in 8930 8931 8932 8934 9430 9434; do for pid in $(lsof -nP -iTCP:$p -sTCP:LISTEN 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR>1{print $2}' | sort -u); do echo "$p pid $pid cwd $(lsof -a -p $pid -d cwd -Fn 2>/dev/null | grep '^n' | cut -c2-80)"; done; done; pgrep -fl 'wrangler dev.*(8930|8934)' | cut -c1-110; cd /Users/adithyamurali/tantra-t299 && git diff cloud/.export-centre.sh | grep '^[+-]' | cut -c1-200

events.text: Restarting the private stack cleanly (a leftover process of my own held a port), then running the probes.

events.name: Bash
events.head: Stop my own leftover stack processes and restart the private stack
events.input: $ pkill -f 'wrangler dev --config wrangler.jsonc --port 893[04]' ; pkill -f 'tantra-t299/cloud/node_modules/.bin/wrangler dev'; for pid in $(pgrep -f 'workerd' ); do c=$(/usr/sbin/lsof -a -p $pid -d cwd -Fn 2>/dev/null | grep '^n' | cut -c2-); case "$c" in /Users/adithyamurali/tantra-t299*) kill $pid;; esac; done; p=$(cat /tmp/t299/runner.pid 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$p" ] && kill $p 2>/dev/null; perl -e 'sleep 3'; for p in 8930 8931 8934 9430 9434; do /usr/sbin/lsof -nP -iTCP:$p -sTCP:LISTEN 2>/dev/null | awk -v p=$p 'NR>1{print p, $1, $2}'; done; cd /Users/adithyamurali/tantra-t299 && git checkou

events.name: Bash
events.head: See how run-chain orders the four probes and simulator resets
events.input: $ cd /Users/adithyamurali/tantra-t299 && grep -n 'SIM_RESET\|probe-domain-chain\|probe-day1\|probe-day2\|probe-stack' app/scripts/run-chain.sh | cut -c1-220

events.name: Bash
events.head: Run the four probes against the private simulator stack
events.input: $ cd /Users/adithyamurali/tantra-t299/app && set -a && . /tmp/t299/keys.env && set +a && export SIM_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8932 FUNNEL_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8934 && ADMIN="http://127.0.0.1:8930/admin/enter?k=$ADMIN_KEY" && for s in "domain-chain d0" "day1 d1" "day2 d2" "stack -"; do set -- $s; if [ "$2" = "-" ]; then node scripts/probe-$1.mjs "$ADMIN" > /tmp/t299/r-$1.log 2>&1; else node scripts/probe-$1.mjs "$ADMIN" /tmp/t299/$2 > /tmp/t299/r-$1.log 2>&1; fi; echo "$1 rc $? ok=$(grep -c '^ *\(ok\|PASS\|✓\)' /tmp/t299/r-$1.log) fail=$(grep -ci 'fail' /tmp/t299/r-$1.log) :: $(tail -1 /tmp/t299/r-$

events.name: Bash
events.head: Read the probe results
events.input: $ cat /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-adithyamurali-tantra-redesign/c0866261-86dc-4827-b9e5-34a16bff8b37/tasks/bfnreqdx1.output | cut -c1-300; for f in domain-chain day1 day2 stack; do echo "## $f"; grep -i 'fail\|error\|timeout' /tmp/t299/r-$f.log | sed -E 's/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{28,}/***/g' | head -6 | cut -c1-240; done

events.name: Bash
events.head: Find the probe logs and see why node crashed
events.input: $ ls -la /tmp/t299/ | cut -c1-120 | head -30; ls /tmp/t299/*.log 2>/dev/null; for f in /tmp/t299/*day1*.log /tmp/t299/*d1*.log; do [ -f "$f" ] && { echo "## $f"; tail -15 "$f" | sed -E 's/[A-Za-z0-9_-]{28,}/***/g' | cut -c1-240; }; done
